title: Frog 1
explanation: The cost to reach stone i only depends on how you reached stone i−1 or i−2, so a 1D table over stones is enough.
traps: Greedily taking the cheaper next jump is not optimal.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i] = minimum total cost to reach stone i
dp[i][j] = minimum cost to go from stone i to stone j
options.why: N² states (1e10) and you only ever start from stone 1.

options.text: dp[h] = minimum cost to reach a stone of height h
options.why: Heights don't identify stones, and the order of stones matters.

options.text: dp[i] = number of ways to reach stone i
options.why: That counts paths; the problem asks for a minimum cost.

extraLayers.explanation: The only thing the future needs to know is the best cost to stand on stone i.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.why: That's the counting recurrence (Fibonacci), not a minimum cost.

options.text: dp[i] = min over all j < i of dp[j] + |h_i − h_j|
options.why: That allows jumps of any length (that's Frog 2 with K = N); here only +1 and +2 are allowed.
Mixes two different predecessors: the +2 jump doesn't start from stone i−1.

extraLayers.explanation: You arrive at i from i−1 or i−2; take the cheaper of the two.
